name: Header
summary: Header sections for the AhaSlides marketing sites: four Hero Pink banners, nineteen heroes and six page headers, each layout with its own name, preview and paste-and-run code.
highlights: Twenty-nine layouts on one page: the Hero Pink banners, the heroes and the page headers, each with its own labelled preview and code

Most layouts add an Accent background, the pale pink bgAccent surface laid over white by the layout's own --accent class, beside White and Vivid Pink; the Hero Pink, Hero Pale Pink and brand layouts keep their own switches and have no Accent because they are already coloured

An optional G2 reviews row (the G2 logo in a white card, five stars, 4.8 and the review count), on by default, on the 22 layouts whose copy block holds the buttons; a G2 reviews switch next to the width and surface switches turns it off on the preview

Five multi-image heroes show several photos at once, each a different arrangement and transition: Hero photo stack (fanned cards that spread on hover), Hero bento collage (a square bento of four), Hero image marquee (a full-width row that loops like the Logos strip, with a Pause button), Hero slideshow (crossfading photos picked with Carousel dots) and Hero floating images (tilted pairs around centred copy). The marquee and slideshow controls come from lib/marketing-motion.js, and every movement stops under reduced motion, print and data-aha-motion="off"
layoutsIntro: Each layout is its own block: the class names below are scoped per layout, so any number of them can sit in one page.

guidance.title: Choosing a header
guidance.intro: Pick the header from the goal of the page, then check the points below. The layouts further down carry a "Use for" line.

points.title: One goal, one primary button
points.text: Each page has one goal and one primary button: one Vivid Pink primary and at most one white secondary. Never two primaries, as the Button rule allows one primary per view. On the solid Vivid Pink state the button is variant="secondary"; on White, the Accent and the Pale Pink (Vivid Pink at 5%) states it is the primary. The per-state switch is the data-variant-<state> hook on the button, so paste the snippet for the surface you use.

points.title: Layout by page goal
points.text: Sign-ups (home, campaign, landing): a hero with a built-in email field, which is Hero split image 01, Hero color card 04 or Hero card mockup 08. Use Hero split form 01 only when you need more than an email. Feature pages: Hero screen mockup 01 to 05, and Hero iPhone mockup 03 for the audience or mobile story. Content and listing pages (blog, templates, help): the page headers, which carry no button on purpose; Header space between buttons brand only when the page has one clear action. Brand or campaign banners: the Hero Pink family. Event, community, brand and culture pages with several real photos: the multi-image heroes (Hero photo stack, Hero bento collage, Hero image marquee, Hero slideshow, Hero floating images).

points.title: Copy
points.text: Write an outcome-led headline of about ten words or fewer and a one-sentence lead. Label the button with a verb and the outcome. Put a risk reducer under the button, for example "Free plan, no card needed".

points.title: Above the fold
points.text: The headline, the button and the visual are visible without scrolling at 1280 by 720 and on mobile. Use a real AhaSlides screenshot, not a stock photo. The badge slot carries news or a short label, not decoration. For proof, keep the G2 reviews row (the G2 logo, stars and the 4.8 rating), which sits under the button on 22 of the layouts and is on by default. In the vertical Hero Pink layouts the image is shown whole at its own ratio at every width, never cropped with object-fit cover (rule W6): supply the screenshot at the ratio you want shown.

points.title: Colour
points.text: Colour rule 3.5 keeps the first screen of a product-app screen white, but a web page built from full-width sections may open with a Vivid Pink header (it is one of the two Vivid Pink sections of rule 3.4). Follow it with a full white section, never another coloured one. A Vivid Pink header always carries the DS Splash background (right when the copy is on the left, centre when it is centred or fills the width), never a flat pink fill or hand-drawn hooks.

points.title: One H1 per page
points.text: A page has one h1. If a second hero sits on the page, its headline becomes an h2.

points.title: Measure
points.text: Track the click on the primary button. A/B test the headline before you change the layout.

points.title: Background
points.text: Most layouts have a White / Accent / Vivid Pink switch: add the layout's own --accent class (for example aha-header-section-hero-split-image-01--accent) to lay the pale pink Accent background (bgAccent) over white. Accent and Vivid Pink are alternatives, never combined. The Hero Pink, Hero Pale Pink and brand header layouts keep their own switches and have no Accent, because they are already coloured surfaces. Never place an Accent header next to another coloured section.

points.title: Hero video
points.text: A hero can carry a video instead of the image (the optional Video slot below, off by default): a real <video> with controls, a poster that is a real screenshot, an English captions track and a download link as fallback. It never autoplays, never loops and never starts with sound, so it is safe under prefers-reduced-motion; the native controls are keyboard reachable. The video box takes the clip's own aspect ratio from the width and height attributes (set them to the clip's real pixel size), so a wide 2.12:1 demo and a 16:9 clip both fill the box with no dark bands and no crop; a height cap keeps a tall clip from taking over the hero.

layouts.name: Hero slideshow
layouts.summary: Copy on the left, four 4:3 photos in one frame on the right that crossfade (--aha-motion-viz-enter, --aha-ease-in-out) when a dot is picked. The dots follow the Carousel pattern (16 × 4 px, the current one 28 px wide in Vivid Pink) inside 24 × 24 px buttons, so each is a full tap target and reachable with Tab. lib/marketing-motion.js wires the dots. Autoplay is off: data-aha-autoplay on the slideshow turns it on (every 5 s, paused while hovered or focused, never under reduced motion or data-aha-motion="off"), but the Website motion rule (W9) does not allow an autoplaying carousel, so add it only with design sign-off.
layouts.useFor: Pages that need to show several product moments in the space of one hero image, the first one strong enough to stand alone.
